ibd-a88908df340c714d-q6:b.ii.text: In the Earth frame the signal is emitted at (t = 50 y, x = 30 ly) and received at (t = 80 y, x = 0). Thus Δt = 30 y and Δx = −30 ly. With γ = 1.25, Δt′ = γ(Δt − vΔx/c²) = 1.25[30 − 0.60(−30)] = 60 years. The events occur at different positions, so a proper-time shortcut cannot be used for this interval.

ibd-996809f014b31dce-q1:d.text: The impact speed read from the graph is about 9.5 m s⁻¹. Taking upwards as positive, Δv = 7.8 − (−9.5) = 17.3 m s⁻¹. Impulse gives F T = mΔv, so T = (2.7 × 10⁻³ × 17.3)/1.1 ≈ 0.042 s. The stated force is already the resultant force.

ibd-7c37430fd5ce856d-q4:whole.text: The journey takes 2000/(0.98 × 3.0 × 10⁸) ≈ 6.8 μs in the ground frame. Without time dilation this is about three mean lifetimes, so only a small fraction would survive. Time dilation increases the mean lifetime in this frame to γτ₀ = 5.0 × 2.2 = 11 μs, allowing a much larger fraction to reach the ground. The observed number of muons supports the dilated lifetime; a mean lifetime is not a fixed expiry time for every particle.

ibd-7c37430fd5ce856d-q9:b.text: The entropy is greatest at B. During the isothermal expansion A → B the gas absorbs heat, increasing its entropy. Cooling B → C reduces its entropy. The reversible adiabatic path C → A has no entropy change, so SA = SC < SB.

ibd-b3e86d458430f237-q4:whole.text: Maxwell’s theory identifies light as an electromagnetic wave with a definite propagation speed in vacuum. Special relativity takes this vacuum speed c to be the same for every inertial observer, independently of the motion of the source. The electromagnetic laws therefore have the same form in all inertial frames.

ibd-10bb8b2b4d47787b-q17:whole.text: Considering motion alone, a clock moving at speed v in an inertial frame accumulates proper time dτ = dt/γ. A higher speed means a larger γ and less elapsed time on that clock. For aircraft and ground clocks, compare both speeds in the same inertial frame: their different speeds, including the effect of Earth’s rotation, produce different accumulated times. Eastward and westward journeys need not give the same comparison with the ground clock.

ibd-90c7459b463b96a2-qB2:whole.text: For a head-on approach, the alpha particle’s kinetic energy becomes electric potential energy at its closest point. E = 5.0 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.0 × 10⁻¹³ J. Set E = k(2e)(79e)/r. Thus r = (8.99 × 10⁹ × 158 × (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)²)/(8.0 × 10⁻¹³) ≈ 4.6 × 10⁻¹⁴ m.

fep-3fb598f3b26e81bc-qD1:whole.text: Yes: the two arrivals at Hermann occur at the same place and at the same time, so they are a single coincident event. Here Δx = 0 and Δt = 0; a Lorentz transformation gives Δt′ = γ(Δt − vΔx/c²) = 0. This does not establish that the two spatially separated emissions were simultaneous in every frame.

fep-1abed29a095af17f-qD4:whole.text: The gain mgh accounts only for the useful increase in gravitational potential energy. The body also uses chemical energy for metabolism and internal movement, and transfers thermal energy to its surroundings. Its conversion of chemical energy to useful mechanical work is less than 100% efficient, so more food energy is needed.

fep-0401f909c25295c4-qG1:whole.text: The landings are not simultaneous in Simon’s frame. In the ground frame Simon moves towards the light from the front end and away from the light from the rear end. In Simon’s frame light still travels at c and the midpoint is equally far from the two ends; the earlier arrival from the front therefore corresponds to an earlier landing at the end towards which the carriage moves.

fep-49b3d1fd7578318d-qG2:whole.text: Nino does not see the two hits as simultaneous. In the ground frame the train moves to the right: L moves towards the left-going pulse while R moves away from the right-going pulse. Both pulses travel at c in that frame, so the pulse reaches L first. Clare, at rest at the train’s midpoint, measures equal travel times to the two ends.

fep-13a7c557ac9687da-qB4:1.h.text: Work delivered per cycle = power/cycles per second = 8400/40 = 210 J. Since η = W/Qin = 0.40, the heat supplied per cycle is Qin = 210/0.40 = 525 J.

fep-6d03205b0ef8f56e-qC1:b.vi.text: The turbine supplies mechanical power 600/0.75 = 800 MW. Its thermal efficiency is 800/2400 = 1/3. For the ideal Carnot limit, η = 1 − Tc/Th. Thus Th = 300/(1 − 1/3) = 450 K.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:a.text: Entropy measures the number of microscopic arrangements compatible with a macroscopic state. Greater spreading of energy among available states corresponds to greater entropy; “greater disorder” is a qualitative description of this.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.d.text: Entropy measures the number of microscopic arrangements compatible with a macroscopic state. Greater spreading of energy among available states corresponds to greater entropy; “greater disorder” is a qualitative description of this.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:b.text: The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. Equivalently, ΔSsystem + ΔSsurroundings ≥ 0: it is zero for an ideal reversible process and positive for an irreversible process.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.e.text: The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. Equivalently, ΔSsystem + ΔSsurroundings ≥ 0: it is zero for an ideal reversible process and positive for an irreversible process.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:c.text: The egg is not an isolated system. Its local increase in organization is accompanied by transfers of energy and matter to its surroundings. The increase in the surroundings’ entropy compensates for any decrease in the egg’s entropy, so the total entropy does not decrease.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.f.text: The water’s entropy decreases as it becomes a more ordered solid. Freezing releases latent heat into the surroundings, increasing their entropy. The total entropy change is non-negative: zero in the ideal reversible limit, and positive in an actual irreversible process.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:a.text: Draw an arrow Qin from the hot reservoir into the engine, an arrow W from the engine to useful work, and an arrow Qout from the engine to the cold reservoir. fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.i.text: D → A is the isothermal compression: volume decreases along the lower-temperature isotherm.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.ii.text: C → D is the adiabatic expansion: volume increases without heat transfer, and the gas cools.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.iii.text: Work is done on the gas during D → A and A → B. Both are compression stages, so the volume decreases.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.iv.text: Heat enters during B → C and leaves during D → A. The other two stages are adiabatic and have no heat transfer.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:c.text: The area enclosed by the cycle on the pressure–volume diagram is the net work delivered in one cycle. The clockwise direction corresponds to positive net work done by the gas.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:d.text: With the same hot-reservoir temperature, a colder outdoor reservoir in winter reduces Tc/Th. The maximum efficiency η = 1 − Tc/Th therefore increases. Both temperatures must be in kelvin.

fep-48711ac5ebc72e6f-q8:whole.text: D. Translational equilibrium requires zero resultant force. The object can be at rest or moving with constant velocity; equilibrium does not require zero velocity.

fep-48711ac5ebc72e6f-q13:whole.text: A. The tension is perpendicular to the instantaneous displacement, so W = F s cos 90° = 0. It changes the direction of the velocity without changing the kinetic energy.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q11:whole.text: B. Newton’s third law gives equal-magnitude, opposite-direction interaction forces. The objects can have different accelerations because their masses differ.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q12:whole.text: D. Useful lifting work = weight × height = 1.5 × 10³ × 10 = 1.5 × 10⁴ J. The supplied energy is useful work/efficiency = (1.5 × 10⁴)/0.20 = 7.5 × 10⁴ J.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q12:whole.correction: Original asks for work done raising the object but omits the useful-work value from the options. Clarified that the requested quantity is input energy; quantities and choices preserved.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q13:whole.text: A. The total momentum of Joe and the ball remains zero when external impulse is negligible: they acquire equal and opposite momenta. Their total kinetic energy increases because chemical energy is converted into motion.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q14:whole.text: C. Velocity is tangent to the circular path, upwards at the position shown. Acceleration points towards the centre, to the left. Constant speed does not mean zero acceleration.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q15:whole.text: D. Absolute temperature is proportional to the mean random translational kinetic energy of the particles. It is not a measure of their maximum kinetic energy or the total energy of the sample.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:a.text: AB is isothermal. At A, pV = (2.0 × 10⁵)(5.0 × 10⁻³) = 1000 J; at B, pV = (5.0 × 10⁵)(2.0 × 10⁻³) = 1000 J. For a fixed amount of ideal gas, equal pV means equal temperature. The steeper curve AC is the adiabatic compression.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:c.text: Estimate the area between AC and AB over the compression from 5.0 × 10⁻³ to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. The work done on the gas is greater along AC by approximately 1.6 × 10² J. A small grid square represents (0.1 × 10⁵ Pa)(0.1 × 10⁻³ m³) = 1 J, so counting the enclosed squares gives the estimate.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:d.text: For the adiabatic compression, Q = 0. Work done on the gas increases its internal energy. Since the internal energy of a fixed amount of ideal gas depends on temperature, its temperature rises.

fep-314acbf92ebc17fd-qE2:a.iii.text: Use the boiler as the hot reservoir and the condenser as the cold reservoir. The maximum thermal efficiency is ηmax = 1 − Tcondenser/Tboiler, with both temperatures expressed in kelvin.

fep-314acbf92ebc17fd-qE2:b.i.text: The high-temperature energy supplied at the boiler is higher-quality energy. The thermal energy rejected at the colder condenser is lower-quality energy because a smaller fraction can be converted into useful work.

fep-314acbf92ebc17fd-qE2:b.ii.text: Energy is conserved, but some is transferred to the cold reservoir as thermal energy. This dispersed, lower-temperature energy is less available for conversion to useful work, so its quality has decreased.

fep-314acbf92ebc17fd-qE2:c.text: An irreversible process increases total entropy as energy becomes more dispersed. More of the conserved energy is then unavailable for useful work. Increased entropy describes this loss of energy quality, not destruction of energy.

fep-5a4740c29cc82303-qC1:a.text: A heat engine takes energy from a hot reservoir, converts some into work and rejects the rest to a cold reservoir. A heat pump uses supplied work to transfer energy from a colder reservoir to a warmer one. Their useful outputs are different: work for the engine, transferred thermal energy for the pump.

fep-5a4740c29cc82303-qA2:whole.text: Starting at A at t = 0 with period 0.80 s, the object is at A at 0 and 0.80 s, at B at 0.40 s, and at the equilibrium position E at 0.20 and 0.60 s. Acceleration has maximum magnitude upwards at A, maximum magnitude downwards at B, and is zero at E, since a = −ω²x.

fep-aae5041a67de03ff-qB4:1.i.text: For one isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, ΔU = 0 and all the heat supplied becomes work. This is not a complete repeating cycle: the gas has expanded. Returning it to its initial state requires compression and, in an engine cycle, heat rejection. A cyclic engine cannot turn all of its heat input into net work without rejecting heat.

fep-166845b0058d8d48-qC1:a.text: Draw thermal energy QC flowing from the room into the heat pump, work W flowing from the motor into the pump, and thermal energy QH flowing from the pump to the outside air. The QH arrow is the largest, since QH = QC + W.

fep-166845b0058d8d48-qC1:b.text: Conservation of energy gives QH = QC + W: the energy delivered outside equals the energy removed from the room plus the work supplied to the pump.

fep-166845b0058d8d48-qC1:c.text: Yes. The thermal energy removed from the room can exceed the work supplied. The pump transfers existing thermal energy rather than converting work alone into the entire heat output; QH = QC + W still holds.

fep-166845b0058d8d48-qC1:d.text: For the ideal reversible pump, QC/W = Tc/(Th − Tc) = 280/(320 − 280) = 7. With 500 W of input power, the maximum rate of thermal energy removal is 7 × 500 = 3500 W.

fep-166845b0058d8d48-qC1:e.text: There is no violation: work is supplied to move thermal energy from the colder room to the warmer outside air. The second law forbids this transfer as the sole result of a process, without another change. The total entropy of room, surroundings and power supply does not decrease.
